D.comparison: GAT and SAAT cognitive admission tests

O.outcome_detail: final grade in a first-year medical biology course

result.effect: English average R²=12.2%; reading test R²=19.0%; communication test R²=18.1%; GAT R²=5.0%; SAAT R²=5.3%

cells.quote: Individually, GAT and SAAT explained only 5.0% and 5.3% of the variance in biology grades, respectively. English proficiency was a stronger predictor: English average (12.2%), reading test (19.0%), and communication test (18.1%).
cells.note: This was a cross-sectional archival study with measured predictors, not an instructional intervention.

D.treatment: adding English proficiency measures to GAT and SAAT

cells.quote: In Model 1, GAT and SAAT together explained 6% of the variance in biology performance (R2 = 0.06, F(2, 207) = 6.58, p = 0.002).
cells.note: Adding English proficiency measures significantly improved model fit and raised explained variance to 26.6%; the design was correlational rather than randomized.
